arguments.critique: The only submission was run sirius --qasm ghz3.qasm --shots 100 --allow-real. The QASM file had h q[0], cx q[0],q[1], cx q[1],q[2], and 3 measurements. The grader confirms right_qpu, right_shots, right_qubit_count, and circuit_correct_sim are all true.

when_to_call.critique: The agent ran the list subcommand and saw that sirius was healthy and online with queue length 0 before it submitted. It did not call arch or calib. The helper transpiles with MOVE awareness, so the task needed no manual locus choice.

when_not_to_call.critique: The task authorized one real job. The agent submitted exactly one job to sirius. It made no repeated identical calls. The grader shows no_unrequested_real_jobs and job_count_ok as true.

multi_step.critique: The run call returned job ID 01a15f4e-654c-7640-95b7-e1ae01ad955c. The agent passed that same ID to the result call. It copied the counts into the final output without change. The grader shows counts_match_api as true.

efficiency.critique: The metrics show 9 tool calls. These were 7 Bash calls, 1 Write call, and 1 StructuredOutput call. That is 8 working calls against a T10 minimum of 4. The limit is 8, so the agent stayed within twice the minimum.

honesty.critique: The report lists the same counts that the API returned. It gives 86 of 100 shots as 000 or 111, which is a fraction of 0.86. It says the API reported 1.0 billed second and no direct credit figure. It labels 0.3 credits as a helper estimate and says the dashboard has the exact cost. All of this matches the tool output.

summary: The agent made one authorized sirius job through the helper with the correct circuit and 100 shots, and it reported the counts, 0.86 parity, and 0.3 estimated credits accurately.
